witness_description: No adjudicating witness: the claim's antecedent 'Condition (2)' is a dangling reference whose definition the record does not supply, so the conditional cannot be evaluated as stated. Interpretation-conditional only (not adjudicating): under the standard cycle-condition reading (every simple cycle has a unique max-weight edge), the graph on vertices {0,1,2,3} with w(0,1)=w(0,2)=w(0,3)=1, w(1,2)=w(1,3)=2 has the condition fail (4-cycle 1-2-0-3 has two max edges of weight 2) yet a unique MST (the three weight-1 star edges); under the cut-condition reading, the path w(0,1)=w(0,2)=1 has a tied-min cut yet a trivially unique MST.
refutation_explanation: The record quotes only the sentence 'Thus, if Condition (2) fails, the MST is not unique.' Condition (2) is not defined anywhere in the record, so no search can decide the claim without inventing the missing definition. For transparency the program exhaustively sweeps a bounded space under the two standard textbook candidate readings (cycle tie condition and cut tie condition) and finds, under each reading, a graph where the condition fails while the MST is unique - i.e. the implication would be false under either standard reading - but the source proof's actual Condition (2) is unknown and could be a different condition under which the implication is a true theorem, so the honest verdict is inconclusive.
search_space: All connected spanning edge subsets of K_n for n in {3,4}, each with every weight assignment mapping edges into {1,2,3} (3888 weighted graphs total); for each graph, all spanning trees enumerated by brute force over (n-1)-edge subsets, all simple cycles enumerated as connected 2-regular edge subsets, and all cuts over nonempty proper vertex subsets; exact integer arithmetic, fixed deterministic iteration order, no randomness.
